name: Travis Kim
biography: Hello! I am a sophomore at Northwestern University pursuing a B.A. in Philosophy and Cognitive Science with a minor in Computer Science. I am a Research Assistant for Professor Bharath Chandrasekaran and Dr. Zhe-chen Guo in the SoundBrain Lab, a Research Fellow at SPAR Research mentored by Matthew Khoriaty, and a Student Researcher for Professor Haoqi Zhang in Design, Technology, and Research at Northwestern. I am also writing a sci-fi novella funded by Northwestern's Office of Undergraduate Research and mentored by Professor Michelle Huang. My technical research interests are in the ways people and neural networks interact, specifically in the domains of speech perception, LLM alignment, and human-AI collaboration. My philosophical interests concern the rigid framing of people and modern compute as essentially separate beings despite their many imbrications, at times delving into AI safety, drawing on posthuman theory, Asian American literature, and some virtue ethics. You can find my resume [here], a recent publication [here], and a sewing project [here].

research.title: Humans can learn to detect AI voice clones

links.label: Project description
links.description: Abstract: Recent advancements have led to improvements in artificially generated voice clones increasingly indistinguishable from human speech. Motivated by the present and growing threat of AI voice fraud, we seek to determine whether humans can be taught to detect voice clones. In two online studies, human listeners (N = 480) identified whether voices were human or AI-generated (N = 221,776 total decisions). Using a rigorous pre-post design, we examined listener performance before and after brief (~20 minute) feedback-based training. Training successfully improved people’s ability to detect AI voices and improvements generalized to untrained voices. We replicated these effects in a second experiment and investigated the individual differences that predict better AI detection ability. Accounting for other variables, those with better speech categorization consistency – a stable trait-level measure of stability of speech representations – were better at detecting AI and had larger improvements after training. Together, these results reframe AI voice clone detection as a learnable speech-specific expertise.

research.title: Cochlear Implant Sound Quality Matching
research.credit: In collaboration with Stephen Dennison, Katelyn Berg, and Michael Dorman.

links.label: Project description
links.description: Cochlear implant (CI) patients with one non-CI ear and one-CI ear are uniquely able to match the perceived sound quality from their CI ear by applying filters to the sound perceived in their non-CI ear. This project is in collaboration with Stephen Dennison, Katelyn Berg, and Michael Dorman, expanding on [Dennison et al., 2026](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/neuroscience/articles/10.3389/fnins.2026.1798569/full) to create a more streamlined, intuitive process for CI matching with a software that can run on any web browser. A broader goal of this project is to identify perceptual links between adjectives of sound quality and modifications of acoustic effects and filters.

projects.title: 12oz Navy Selvedge Jeans
projects.description: This was my first project back in nearly a year, having not sewed much in the past academic year. I was glad to see that my muscle memory was still there, and I was able to walk through all of the steps without making any large blunders. This project took me around 8 hours, but two of those hours were in fixing the pattern, so I feel more confident in my skills now, and I wager I may be able to make a proper pair of jeans in 5 hours. This was my first time using a selvedge fabric over 32 inches wide which was perfect, as I could fit two pattern pieces on one width rather than alternating them and wasting fabric with the leftover width, as I would have done on thinner fabrics. I filmed a short video of the process.

projects.title: 12oz Blackened Blue Striped Cotton Denim
projects.description: This fabric was too expensive for my own good, but it was too visually appealing for me to not buy at least enough for a pair of jeans. The website says it's 12oz, but it's probably more like 9-10 based on how thin it is. This is not selvedge, but I used a selvedge pattern and mimicked the clean edge with bias tape on the outseam (I do not have a serger). I'm pretty happy with how these turned out, though I think I used a zipper that's too long. Next time I will cut the zipper so it is 5 inches and not 7.

projects.title: 11oz Hickory Selvedge Denim
projects.description: This was definitely the most experimental of the pieces I've sewn. I took heavy, heavy inspiration from [this pair of pants](https://www.reversible.com/shopping/men/item/kapital-kapital-10oz-hickoree-stripe-painter-port-baggy-pants-champetre-remake-824342913), but looking back I'm realizing that they have a much lighter wash and wear to their design. I think the fabric I used was a bit too strong visually, and I don't wear them as often as I would like to because of that. I still have some more of this fabric, so I plan to lightly bleach it to subdue the dark blue stripes a bit more before sewing again.

projects.description: This fabric was really pleasant to work with because it was already sanforized (meaning less math to figure out how much the pattern will shrink), and the fabric itself light compared to the other denims I use, making it easier to punch through the thicker sections of denim. Looking back I wish I made the pattern a little less baggy, but this was a good test of a new pattern.

interests.blurb: I have been sewing since 2024, focusing mostly on jeans. Since then, I have made around ten pairs for my friends and self. My machine is the Bernette b37.

I mostly take photos for fun on hikes and with friends, though I occasionally shoot freelance events. I primarily use a Panasonic Lumix S5 with either the Pentax Super Takumar 50mm f/1.4 lens or the Sigma 24-70mm f/2.8 DG DN II Art Lens.

Some of my favorite authors are Morrison, Faulkner, Ishiguro, McCarthy, Woolf, and Dostoevsky. My favorite book is *As I Lay Dying* by Faulkner. You can see my book reviews and what I'm currently reading [here](https://www.goodreads.com/user/show/165804766-travis-kim) and some of my short story publications below.

I've been competing in powerlifting since 2023. I am coached by [Sean Collins](https://www.sincerepl.com/our-team-v2). A significant achievement: I was [national champion](https://www.openpowerlifting.org/u/traviskim) in 2024. I am also the founder and president of [Northwestern University's Barbell Club](https://www.instagram.com/northwesternbarbell/).
